# Boot-level dispersion, sample-size-robust

*Generated by `analysis/boot_statistics.py`. Do not edit by hand.*

Coefficient of variation is the comparable statistic here. A max/min **range grows with n by construction**, so ranges from arms with different boot counts cannot be compared; they are shown for continuity with earlier revisions and should not be used for inference.

## Acceptance ($\tau$) under repeated identical boots

Boot-variance probes only: one fixed prompt set replayed on every boot. Grid records are excluded because their repeats draw different prompts by design, which measures prompt variance rather than boot variance.

- n = 12, mean 4.1055, sd 0.0256
- **CV = 0.62%**
- 95% CI on the mean: [4.0893, 4.1218]
- Minimum detectable effect at this n, ~80% power: **1.74%** of the mean
- max/min range: 1.38% (was reported as a 1.32% "noise floor" at n=4; the range **grew** with n, which is what ranges do)

- Distinct values observed: [4.0914, 4.1479]. Acceptance is near-deterministic given fixed prompts rather than continuously noisy, which is a further reason "noise floor" was the wrong description.

## Why the range was not comparable

DFlash default at full n=23 has max/min 2.96x. Subsampling the same data to n=8, 200 draws, gives a mean max/min of **2.38x** (observed 1.57x to 2.96x). The eager arm was reported at n=8. Roughly a fifth of the headline contrast was sample size, not behaviour.
